description: Work-in-progress fork of VIctory: getting an Xbox Series title to render and run on a Windows PC. No game files.
readme_excerpt:
# VIctory fork (work in progress)

A work-in-progress fork of [VIctory](https://github.com/Marvisak/VIctory), a
compatibility layer that runs an Xbox Series title natively on Windows from
files the user supplies. This fork follows upstream
`main` and adds fixes aimed at one goal: getting the game's world to render
correctly and playably on one particular PC.

**This repository contains no game files, code or assets.** You need your own
copy of the game. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the game's
developer or publisher.

## Credits

- **[VIctory](https://github.com/Marvisak/VIctory)** by Marvisak and its
  contributors is the base of everything here: the loader, the runtime
  services, the Direct3D 12 back end and the shader recompiler. Licensed
  GPL-3.0-or-later; so is this fork. Upstream's history is kept intact below
  the single commit that carries this fork's changes.
- **[XCL](https://github.com/ivall/xcl)** by ivall and its contributors
  (GPL-2.0-only) was used as a reference for how the same title behaves under
  another layer. Fixes inspired by it were written anew in VIctory's code.
- The guard over every view of a memory page is code by **myokex**
  ([victory-amd](https://github.com/myokex/victory-amd), commit `c6dc4d8`), which
  adapts pull request #115 here by Spexivus, its correction by joroyt and a part of
  VIctory #1122 by tightfall. The read-beside fix for kernel reads into title
  memory is by **Joshua Odom** (commit `10ea38e` of the same fork family). Both
  are carried here unchanged apart from one merge conflict.
- This fork's changes were developed with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code).

## Status of this fork (2026-11-25)

**Not playable yet: 2.5 to 4 frames per second, and shadowed areas are black.**
Tested on one machine: Windows 11, Intel i7-14700KF, NVIDIA RTX 4070 12 GB,
32 GB RAM. The Series X profile is used throughout.

| Stage | State in this fork |
|-------|--------------------|
| Boot, menus, start screen | works, 30 fps (as upstream) |
| Opening cutscene | plays from start to finish, in order, lit: title cards, credits cards, night and dusk shots |
| Saves | the game autosaves a checkpoint and loads it again |
| First gameplay scene (the prologue) | renders: characters, textures, sky, sunlit exterior; HUD, pause menu and pad input work |
| Light in shadow | missing: the game's ray-traced bounce light and ray-traced lamp and sun shadows do not run yet, so anything the sun does not hit directly is black |
| Frame rate in the world | 2-4 fps: 420-450 ms per frame by default, 240-350 ms with the newer switches (`VICTORY_RELAY=2`, or `VICTORY_LATE_WAIT=3 VICTORY_WIDE_BACK=1 VICTORY_CARD_BUFFERS_MIN_MB=1 VICTORY_CARD_BUFFERS_MB=1024`); it started at 3-6 seconds per frame |
| Stability | no driver hang or device loss in normal runs (a hang introduced by the wave64 update was found and fixed: its barrier form for 64-lane programs is now off unless `VICTORY_WAVE_WIDE=1`) |

### Newest (2026-11-25, later the same day)

**Update, 2026-11-25 afternoon: what a frame is made of, measured, and two
changes that hold.** First rooms, about 3,850 draws a frame: 104 ms a frame
(9.6 frames a second) with the first two changes below, 97 ms (10.3)
with all of them, from about 120 ms in the morning. Still far from the console's 33 ms.
- How the title paces itself (new meters in `fence.rs` and
  `console_insn.rs`): it never asks for an event. Each frame begins with
  one small submission and a signal, and a title thread then waits for
  that fence value by reading it in memory with `monitorx` / `mwaitx`
  (AMD-only: about 280,000 emulated exceptions a second on an Intel
  processor, all from this wait). The value is set when the layer has
  finished the whole frame before. So a frame is the time the layer needs
  for one frame's burst of submissions plus about 20 ms of the title's

`≤8.8 KB` inline cap · Native diff & UI untouched |

description: An attempt at running GTA VI on PC
readme_excerpt:
# VIctory

Runs Grand Theft Auto VI (Xbox Series X|S) natively on Windows, from files
the user supplies.

The title's x86-64 code runs unchanged inside our process; VIctory supplies
the platform underneath it and converts the title's data, ahead of time where
it can (shaders and pipelines too, see Getting started) and on first use
otherwise. See [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md).

## Status (2026-11-25)

**Not playable yet, but you can get into the game.** The title boots, runs
its menus at its own 30 fps, loads the world, plays the intro cutscene and
reaches the **prologue**, the mission after it, with the graphics fully
displayed, at about **1 frame per second**.

| Stage | State |
|-------|-------|
| Boot, first-boot screens (accessibility, language, settings, legal) | works, 30 fps |
| Intro video with sound | works |
| Start screen, profile and saves | works |
| Loading into the world (about a minute) | works |
| The intro cutscene | plays at about 1 fps (0.9-1.0 s a frame, warm cache, quiet machine): textured and lit characters with whole hair, buildings, sky, depth of field, the title card, credits and interface. Missing: ray-traced shadows and indirect light, the local-light shadow mask. Seen in some shots: a pink band over nearer bodies, a stand-in head on a secondary character for a few frames |
| The prologue | reached; the graphics are fully displayed, at about 1 fps |

In the intro cutscene at 1 fps the opening credits land over other shots than
on a console: they follow the frame count, the shots follow the clock.

Tested on one machine: Windows 11, AMD RX 6700 XT (12 GB).

> **Warning.** Entering the world on a real GPU hung it in earlier builds,
> and Windows then reset the display driver (every monitor goes black for a
> moment). The latest runs, several minutes each in the world, did not, but
> it is not ruled out; a run can also end on a GPU fault (`crashes.log`). A
> diagnostics build with `VICTORY_D3D12_WARP=1` renders on the software
> adapter instead (too slow to reach the world in minutes).

What each part does today and what it still needs:

| Subsystem | Today | Needs |
|-----------|-------|-------|
| Loader | Runs the title's executable and its DLLs in our process; crash reports name the faulting code and are kept in `crashes.log` | – |
| Runtime services | One signed-in offline user, licences, packages, saves that survive a kill at any step, text entry dialog | Speech is silent; the dialog and relaunch are untested live |
| Network | Offline by design: the title cannot reach the network | – |
| Files and streaming | Archives and streamed data read, zlib and BCPack decoded in parallel | Loading is limited by writes into title memory |
| Input | XInput pads, keyboard, keyboard stand-in pad | Trigger rumble |
| Audio | Menu, video and loading sound; XMA voices and Opus streams decode | Reverb is silent; Opus results unverified against the title |
| GPU: menus | Draws, compute and presentation on host D3D12; only changed title memory is copied | Frame pacing drifts on one screen in release builds |
| GPU: world | The scene is drawn and presented: mesh pipelines, indirect execution, views the shaders pick from the heap themselves, title memory read by address, depth written from compute, lists that wait for values other queues write, textures made when a shader first reads them, pipelines pre-built or made by worker threads and kept on disk | The title's ray-tracing structures are never built (no ray-traced shadows or indirect light in the intro cutscene); about 1 s a frame; draws of untranslated shaders are dropped; real queries, depth bounds, HDR and scaling are missing |
| Shaders | Console GPU code recompiled to DXIL, ahead of time (`translate --cache`) or at first use, cached on disk. Menus: all. World: all but under 300 of 24,387 programs | Merged geometry stages (195 programs) and under 100 others; fused multiply-adds follow the host GPU; some compute programs need a GPU with 64-lane wa

description: Xbox Series compatibility layer for Windows - runs console game code natively, reimplements the console system libraries and recompiles RDNA2 shaders to DXIL
readme_excerpt:
Games · Highlights · How it works · Quick start · What works · Controls · Building and usage · Tests · Contributing

# XCL – Xbox Series X|S → Windows compatibility layer XCL is a compatibility layer that runs Xbox Series X|S (GDK) games you own on a Windows PC - in the spirit of Wine/Proton. There is no CPU emulation: the game's x64 code runs natively, and XCL provides its own, independently written implementations of the console system libraries the PC does not have (`kernelx.dll`, XGameRuntime, `d3d12_xs.dll`, …). The console's GPU code (RDNA2 machine code) is recompiled into PC shaders (HLSL → DXIL). > [!IMPORTANT] > XCL works only on unpacked game files you already own. It does not download, decrypt or unpack game packages (XVC / MSIXVC) and contains nothing for circumventing DRM. The repository holds no code, headers or binaries from the console SDK, no keys and no game data; the Windows components XCL relies on (XGameRuntime, XAudio2, D3D12, DXC) come from your own system or the public Windows SDK and are not distributed with XCL.

## Games

| Game | State | What works | Limits | |---|---|---|---| | **Minecraft Preview**
`Microsoft.MinecraftBeta` 1.18.3064.0 | ✅ playable | fully playable | – | | **Unicorn Overlord**
`SEGAofAmericaInc.Pa253b0c1Y` 1.0.0.6 | ✅ playable | fully playable | – | | **Fortnite**
`436609B6.FortniteClient` 2.0.1461.7919 | ✅ works | works fully, as far as the game allows without its online services | the game itself is online-only (multiplayer servers) | | **XDefiant**
`Ubisoft.XDefiant-Game` 1.0.0.186 | ✅ works | works fully, as far as the game allows without its servers | the game's own servers have been shut down | | **A newer retail game** | 🚧 **≈ 60 %**
estimate | starts in ~4 s, runs at a steady 30 fps without a crash, shows its menus and goes on past the first one to its settings; fits a 32 GB machine (~15 GB committed in the menus). With the NVIDIA integration branch ([#2057](https://github.com/xcl-dev/xcl/pull/2057)) it goes on into its 3D world: **~5 fps there** on an RTX 5090 (14 fps on average over a whole 5-minute run, its menus and loading included) |

description: make your macbook's trackpad talk using its haptic motor
readme_excerpt:
```text
────────────────────────  a90.com presents  ─────────────────────────

    _   __ ____      _____  ____   ______ ___     __ __  ______ ____
   / | / // __ \    / ___/ / __ \ / ____//   |   / //_/ / ____// __ \
  /  |/ // / / /    \__ \ / /_/ // __/  / /| |  / ,<   / __/  / /_/ /
 / /|  // /_/ /    ___/ // ____// /___ / ___ | / /| | / /___ / _, _/
/_/ |_/ \____/    /____//_/    /_____//_/  |_|/_/ |_|/_____//_/ |_|

─  haptic voice synthesis  ─────────────────────────────  trackpad  ─
```

**Mute your Mac. Your trackpad will still talk.**

There's no speaker in a MacBook trackpad, just a small haptic motor that taps the glass so you feel a click.
NO SPEAKER drives that motor up to 4,000 times a second, fast enough to make sound you can hear, and turns it
into a voice. It talks, sings, raps, and becomes an instrument under your finger.

One command. About a minute and a half. No speakers used.

[Watch the demo on X](https://x.com/codycollier/status/2124505859883716918), with the sound on.

## 01 / before you start

```text
[ mute your mac ]        it still talks; that's the point
[ put it on a table ]    on your lap it's much quieter
[ hands off the glass ]  until it asks you to touch it
```

**Space** skips a part. **q** or **Ctrl-C** goes to the end.

## 02 / run it

`[ one line ]`

```sh
curl -fsSL a90.com/nospeaker | sh
```

Downloads the latest release to `~/.local/bin/nospeaker` and starts the show. `a90.com/nospeaker` points
to [play.sh](play.sh) in this repo, so you can read what it runs first.

`[ download ]`

Grab `nospeaker.zip` from the [latest release](https://github.com/os6/nospeaker/releases/latest),
unzip it and run `./nospeaker` in Terminal. Signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple.

`[ from source ]`

Needs Xcode or the Command Line Tools (`xcode-select --install`). Builds one program for Apple Silicon
and Intel Macs. Built with only the Command Line Tools, the Intel part needs macOS 13 or later.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/os6/nospeaker
cd nospeaker
./build.sh
./nospeaker
```

## 03 / play with it

```text
./nospeaker "hello there"            say anything
./nospeaker --voice Daniel "hello"   in another macOS voice
./nospeaker --sweep                  a rising tone, 100 Hz to 4 kHz

--dark                               white on black
--plain                              no visuals, plain text
--external                           play through an external Magic Trackpad
```

## 04 / needs

A Force Touch trackpad (built into MacBooks from 2015 on, or a Magic Trackpad 2 or newer), and macOS 12 or
later. Without a Force Touch trackpad, it says so and exits.

```text
tested on

MacBook Pro (Mac17,10)         M5 Max   macOS 27.2.1   everything works
MacBook Pro (MacBookPro15,1)   Intel    macOS 15.7.4   works, built from source
```

Not tested yet: a Magic Trackpad, and versions of macOS older than 15. MultitouchSupport is private, so
older systems may lack the functions it uses, and loudness differs between trackpads. If you try it on another
Mac, open an issue with your model, your macOS version and how it sounded.

## 05 / how it works

```text
say ──▶ formants ──▶ two tones ──▶ motor ──▶ glass
        per 10 ms    F1 + F2       haptics   sound
```

**Why you can hear it.** The trackpad has no speaker, but the motor moves the glass. Driven back and forth
hundreds or thousands of times a second, the glass vibrates fast enough to make sound you can hear. It's quiet
because the motor is built for short taps, not for sound.

**The motor.** `MultitouchSupport` is the private framework macOS uses for the trackpad. Its function
`MTActuationCreateFromDictionary` takes a description of a vibration, a list of sine tones with a frequency,
a strength and a length each, and `MTActuationActuate` plays it on the motor. Apple's public haptics API only
offers three fixed taps.

**The range.** Measured with the MacBook's own microphone, every semitone from 98 Hz to 3,951 Hz: how loud it
is over a quiet room,

description: Native YouTube client for Windows in Rust, with SponsorBlock, DeArrow and Return YouTube Dislike built in
readme_excerpt:
Stream Tube

A native YouTube client for Windows and Linux, written in Rust.
No browser, no ads, no tracking. SponsorBlock, DeArrow and Return YouTube Dislike built in.

## Why I wanted YouTube on my desktop without keeping a browser tab open, and without the ads, autoplaying junk and sponsor reads. The existing options were either Electron apps that eat a gigabyte of RAM or web frontends that break every other week. Stream Tube is a single native app: the UI is drawn on the GPU with [GPUI](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/tree/main/crates/gpui), and video goes through libmpv, so it starts fast and scrolls smoothly even with big feeds. ## What it does **No ads, anywhere** - No pre-roll, mid-roll or overlay ads: the app plays the video stream directly, so YouTube's ads are never loaded - No promoted videos, banners or sponsored cards in Home, search or Shorts - Sponsor reads inside videos are skipped too, with SponsorBlock (below) - Nothing to install or keep updated: it isn't an ad blocker that YouTube can break, ads simply aren't part of how the app plays video **Watching** - Home, Shorts, Subscriptions, Explore categories, channels (including their courses and shows), playlists and search, with search suggestions and your recent searches - A personal Home without an account: "For you" recommends videos related to what you've watched and searched in the app, mixed with new uploads from your subscriptions. Signed in, Home is your own YouTube Home feed - A *Recently uploaded* chip on Home, like youtube.com's: videos from your Home feed and subscriptions uploaded in the last two weeks, newest first - Hover a video title in a grid or list to read the full title - Ctrl+click a link or middle-click a video to open it in a background tab. A video's menu also has *Open in new tab*. Switch with Ctrl+Tab, Ctrl+1…9 or a click. Ctrl+T opens a new tab. Ctrl+W or a middle click on the tab closes it. - Videos made for kids (YouTube Kids) play and download like any other video - Old video annotations are back: notes, speech bubbles and clickable links from YouTube's annotation archive, drawn over the video where they used to be (turn them off in *Settings → Player* or from the player's gear menu) - Arabic, Hebrew and other right-to-left text is shown in the right order - Shorts follow your account's recommendations when you're signed in, or start from the Shorts you watched last - Download the current Short from the vertical player's download button - libmpv player with hardware decoding, codec preference (AV1, VP9 or H.264), 360p up to 4K, enhanced bitrate, speed control (remembered per channel if you want), captions you can style (font, colour, opacity, background and edge, with a live preview), chapters and seek-bar preview thumbnails - A chapters panel beside the player, like youtube.com: click the chapter name in the player bar (or *View all* under the description) to list every chapter with its thumbnail, follow the one playing, and jump to any of them - Timestamps in descriptions and comments seek the video and bring t

# deslop-please

[![slop](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https%3A%2F%2Fraw.githubusercontent.com%2Fdeterministic-machines%2Fdeslop-please%2Fbadges%2Fslop.json)](https://github.com/deterministic-machines/deslop-please/actions/workflows/ci.yml?query=branch%3Amain)
[![test](https://github.com/deterministic-machines/deslop-please/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/deterministic-machines/deslop-please/actions/workflows/ci.yml?query=branch%3Amain)
[![crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/deslop-please.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/deslop-please)

An opinionated linter to remove sloppy code. It follows [*A Philosophy of Software Design*](https://www.amazon.com/Philosophy-Software-Design-John-Ousterhout/dp/1732102201): 
**deep** modules, **narrow** interfaces. 


```bash
cargo install deslop-please
```

```bash
> deslop-please

error[field-leak]: `RunQueue::items` is known outside `RunQueue`: 4 places in 2 modules
  --> src/sched/policy.rs:7:1
  = note: src/sched/policy.rs:7:1: `runqueue::sched::policy::admit`
  = note: src/sched/policy.rs:12:1: `runqueue::sched::policy::next`
  = note: src/sched/report.rs:4:1: `runqueue::sched::report::backlog`
  = note: src/sched/report.rs:8:1: `runqueue::sched::report::drained`
    runqueue::queue::ring::RunQueue
      items ◀━┳━ 2  runqueue::sched::policy
              ┗━ 2  runqueue::sched::report
      also known outside: head
      kept: limit

deslop-please: 65535 errors, well done!
```

### It's not my fault 

Sure, let's just mute them:

```bash
deslop-please --update-allow .deslop-please.allow  
deslop-please --allow .deslop-please.allow 
```

### Add to your `AGENTS.md`

```markdown
-  Run [`deslop-please`](https://github.com/deterministic-machines/deslop-please) to check for sloppy code structure.
-  Errors flagged by `deslop-please` must be fixed from first principles, don't do mechanical moves to hide them.
    - `module-cycle` & `tangle`: what is the indented layer of abstraction? Which module should be at which layer?
    - `field-leak` & `shallow-module`: Why we have these fields/functions at all? What are the patterns of use? Can they be hidden behind a narrow interface? Don't fix each leak one at a time, fix them holistically.
    - Draw a diagram to help user understand the before and proposed after structure.
```

## Why they are sloppy 

They are really just one single idea: **deep** modules, **narrow** interfaces.

Deep modules hide the attention for you and your agents, so you only need to care about the narrow interface.

### module-cycle

![module-cycle: before, modules kinds and socket use each other, though listen, Stream::new and BACKLOG_MOST only form a chain; after, BACKLOG_MOST moves into kinds and only socket uses kinds](docs/module-cycle.svg)


### tangle

![tangle: before, Tasks in kernel and Timers in its child module timers know each other, with no module cycle; after, tick in kernel calls both and Timers no longer knows Tasks](docs/tangle.svg)

### field-leak

![field-leak: before, functions in sched push to, index and bump the items and head of RunQueue; after, they call push, pop and backlog, and only RunQueue works on its fields](docs/field-leak.svg)

### shallow-module


![shallow-module: before, app calls 9 of the 15 functions of store; after, it calls new, load and summary, and the rest are hidden behind them](docs/shallow-module.svg)

Double-click **`FFmpeg Video & Audio Converter 4.1.2.exe`** to launch the application. ## ✨ Features - 🎬 **Video Format Conversion** — Convert video files between popular multimedia formats using the powerful FFmpeg processing engine. - 🎵 **Audio File Conversion** — Transform audio files into different formats while configuring encoding options to suit your needs. - 📦 **Batch Media Processing** — Queue multiple media files and process conversion jobs through a unified desktop workflow. - ⚡ **FFmpeg-Powered Encoding** — Benefit from FFmpeg's extensive codec and container support for flexible video and audio transcoding. - 🎛️ **Custom Encoding Presets** — Choose convenient conversion profiles or customize available parameters for greater control over output files. - 🖥️ **User-Friendly Windows GUI** — Manage media conversion through a graphical interface instead of manually entering terminal commands. - 🔧 **Advanced Conversion Options** — Adjust supported FFmpeg parameters for workflows that require more precise control over encoding. ## 🖼️ Overview ![Features](assets/features.png) ### Supported Media Workflows The application brings common multimedia conversion tasks together in one Windows desktop environment. | Workflow | Purpose | |---|---| | Video conversion | Change video formats and containers | | Audio conversion | Convert audio between supported formats | | Video transcoding | Re-encode media using FFmpeg | | Batch conversion | Process multiple files in sequence | | Preset encoding | Apply predefined conversion settings | | Custom encoding | Configure available FFmpeg options | ### Built Around FFmpeg [FFmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org/) provides the underlying multimedia processing capabilities. The graphical interface helps make these capabilities easier to access without requiring users to memorize FFmpeg command-line syntax. ## 🚀 Usage Getting started with desktop media conversion is straightforward: 1. **Launch the application** — Open the FFmpeg Video & Audio Converter on your Windows PC. 2. **Select source media** — Add the video or audio files you want to convert. 3. **Choose an output format** — Select an available format or conversion profile. 4. **Configure encoding settings** — Adjust supported quality, codec, and other conversion parameters as needed. 5. **Start conversion** — Run the conversion job and allow FFmpeg to process your media. 6. **Find your output files** — Open the destination folder and use your converted media.
